question: The Pakal Dul Hydroelectric Project, currently under construction, is located on which tributary of the Chenab River?
solution:
The correct answer is __ Marusudar River.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pakal Dul Hydroelectric Project is one of the largest hydroelectric projects currently being developed in India.
 
• This project is located on the Marusudar River, which is the largest tributary of the Chenab River.
 
• The Chenab River originates from the Himachal Pradesh region and flows through Jammu & Kashmir before entering Pakistan.
 
• The Marusudar River flows in the Kishtwar district of Jammu & Kashmir and is a key source of water for hydroelectric power generation.
 
• The Pakal Dul project is designed to generate around 1000 MW of electricity, making it a significant contributor to energy security in the region.
 
• It is being developed by Chenab Valley Power Projects Private Limited (CVPPPL), a joint venture between NHPC Limited, JKSPDC, and PTC India Limited.
 
• The project is expected to bring substantial economic benefits, including employment generation and infrastructure development in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Hydroelectric Power in India:

 
 
• India is the 7th largest producer of hydroelectric power globally.
 
• Hydropower projects contribute significantly to India's renewable energy targets.
 
• The government promotes such projects under its National Hydroelectric Policy to ensure sustainable development.
 
 
 
• Chenab River:
 
 
• The Chenab River is one of the five rivers of Punjab and originates from the Himachal Pradesh region.
 
• It is a major river in Jammu & Kashmir and serves as a critical water resource.
 
 
 
• Importance of Hydroelectric Projects:
 
 
• Hydroelectric projects play a vital role in reducing carbon emissions and promoting clean energy.
 
• They also aid in flood control, irrigation, and provide socioeconomic benefits.
